messages:
marie: saw a puzzling tail-latency bump on prod around 16:10 UTC for /v1/generate. token-level chart shows a recurring ~120ms spike for tokens 2-6 on some requests. attaching two sample trace ids: trace/0a1b2c and trace/0a1b2d

sam: nice catch. did you correlate with KV cache hit rate?

marie: I did a quick look — global kv_hit_ratio looks fine overall, but per-request breakdowns show bursts of complete KV cold-starts for a subset of traces. those traces also show kernel fallback from fast-quantized path to reference FP32 kernel.

alex: oof. fallback + kv cold start sounds like a double hit. can you paste a snippet from the trace where the kernel switch happens?

marie: here's the relevant snippet from the token timeline in the trace (copied):

```
TOKEN 003: kernel_select: path=quant_avx2 size=4096 -> latency 3.2ms
TOKEN 004: kv_lookup: miss -> fetch_from_storage 45.8ms
TOKEN 004: kernel_select: detected_overflow -> fallback.fp32_generic -> latency 38.7ms
TOKEN 005: kv_restore: reattach_kv_cache -> 12.4ms
TOKEN 005: emit_token -> 1.1ms
```

sam: that explains the ~120ms window (45.8 + 38.7 + 12.4 ~ 97ms plus overhead). two questions: why did kernel_select trigger fallback mid-request? and why did kv miss happen for those particular requests?

ryan: kernel fallback usually comes from either an unsupported opshape (attention pattern longer than heuristics expect) or from a memory allocation failure on the quantized path. we have a soft-error metric kernel_select.fallback_reason which may have values: [opshape, oom, unsupported_kernel]. do we surface that per-request in the token timeline?

marie: not currently. our token timeline only shows chosen kernel id and per-token latency. no explicit fallback_reason label. i think adding that label + a link to trace would help triage.

jenA: (bot) deploy 2024-07-02/16:05 rolled canary to us-east-1 on runtime-v2.3.7 :rocket:

sam: thanks jena. that canary aligns with the start of anomalies. does v2.3.7 change kernel selection rules or quantization mapping?

jena: v2.3.7 includes the new hybrid-quant path that chooses AVX512 kernels by opshape heuristics. it also changed the memory fallback threshold to be slightly more aggressive to avoid oom.

alex: could that aggressive fallback threshold explain why some sequences switch to fp32 mid-request? we should only fallback pre-token or pre-batch if possible. mid-request swap is expensive.

marie: agree. i think the runtime currently reevaluates kernel choice when encountering large attention windows and may trigger a fallback at token boundary. that logic was added to handle dynamic-length context but it creates these mid-request jumps.

ryan: proposal: add two things to metrics and dashboards:
1) token_latency.breakdown: labels {phase=[kv_lookup,kernel_exec,kernel_reconfig,kv_restore,emit]} with per-token histograms
2) kernel_select.fallback_reason on the request-level metric and a per-token optional label when fallback occurs mid-request

sam: also we need a direct link from the per-request token timeline widget to the tracing UI (trace id). right now you have to copy-paste the id. include a trace_url in the request metadata and surface it as a small "Open trace" button in the dashboard.

jena: adding trace_url to request metadata is fine for hosted. for private deployments we need to make it optional (customers may not have tracing endpoints). we can add trace_url as an opt-in config on the deployment object.

alex: another actionable: KV cold-starts — i suspect the root cause is our cache warmup policy. some of these requests are coming from low-QPS routes that get cached evicted and then get a bursty request (cold-start). the dashboard should have a per-route kv_eviction_rate and last_evicted_timestamp so SREs can spot hot/pathological routes.

marie: APPl: can we surface a "kv_cold_start" boolean in the request meta so the per-request breakdown shows a red badge when true?

ryan: yes and while we're at it, emit a short histogram metric kv_cold_start.latency that captures the storage fetch component separately.

sam: for dashboards: new "Per-request breakdown" panel should include:
- request-level: total_token_latency, kernel_fallback_count, kv_cold_start (bool), trace_url
- token timeline: token_latency.breakdown stacked bars by phase (kv/kernel/emit)
- links: trace_url, logs (if available), raw request payload (redacted)

alex: implementation note: adding per-token label cardinality is expensive. token_latency.breakdown should be a rollup produced by the runtime (already aggregates per-token phases into a single payload) so the metrics backend sees a compact set: per-request token_phase_summaries as JSON blob vs thousands of Prometheus timeseries. then the dashboard parses the blob.

jena: agree, pushing full per-token metrics to Prometheus won't scale. suggest adding a lightweight per-request structured metric to our observability pipeline (Honeycomb/OTLP) with a small JSON field token_phase_summaries: e.g., [{phase:kernel_exec, p50:1.2, p95:3.4}, {phase:kv_lookup, p50:0.2, p95:45.8}]

marie: sounds good. next: alerting. propose an alert rule: if percentile(token_latency.total, 95) for a route increases >30% vs baseline AND kernel_select.fallback_rate for that route > 1% in 10m, create a SEV3 and attach top traces.

sam: add a separate alert for "kv burst cold-starts" when kv_cold_start.count > 10 in 5m for a route.

ryan: i'll prototype the metrics changes in runtime branch perf/trace-link and wire in the token_phase_summaries JSON payload to OTLP. want to push a small dashboard PR after we have telemetry in Canary.

marie: thanks. can someone take ownership for the dashboard widget mockup? i can do the mockup, but need someone to hook up queries.

alex: i'll do the queries and Grafana panels. marie, send mockup before EOD PDT and i'll sync tomorrow.

jena: FYI i've pinned this thread and created a ticket INF-2419 to track: add per-request trace_url + token_phase_summaries + kernel_fallback_reason labels.

marie: perfect. action items summarized:
- ryan: prototype runtime telemetry (branch perf/trace-link)
- alex: grafana queries + hook up mockup once telemetry exists
- marie: dashboard mockup + attach sample traces
- sam: write alert rules draft (kv cold-start + fallback spike)
- jena: INF ticket and deployment opt-in config for trace_url

alex: ping me when the branch is up, i'll grab a canary and run synthetic traces to validate. :thumbsup:

marie: closing loop — thanks everyone, we'll reconvene after the canary results. :white_check_mark:
